title: The Home evaluation suite: written requests, a reader of what Home understood, three arms and a gate
request: Make the Home agent more intelligent: a chat where people describe their problem and Home understands it, gets more context, and routes them to the right solution, whether they want a model, a data analysis, data manipulation, business analysis or BI. Plan every gap, then start; the first package measures today's Home before anything changes.
spec: Package H1 of Phase H in docs/guides/AGENTIC_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md: written requests across six tracks with gold tracks, fields and exits, planted traps, three arms, a gate written before any run with a model, today's Home scored on dev as the baseline.
plan: Read the Home agent (draft/chat.py, plan.py, pack.py, workflow.py, pipeline.py), its tests, and the analyst measurement (agent_eval/analyst) whose shape the suite copies: splits with a sealed fingerprint, arms, scoring, gate, CLI, campaign record.

Write the tests first: the splits' mix, the sealed fingerprint, Persian-aware scoring, the reader's checks on a hand-made draft, today's Home scored without a model, the plain arm, the plan of a live run.
Seeded invented tables (sales, customers, bookings) with planted cleaning work and no lifetime_spend or booking_margin column.
Seventy-two written requests (dev and sealed), six per track per split, Persian and mixed, multi-track, six traps, each with gold tracks, fields and exit.

The runner: the real HomeAgent and the real draft pipeline in a throwaway store, questions answered I'm not sure, the finished draft read; the plain arm's prompt as a file; the gate; the CLI with a plan by default and a cap for a priced model.
Score today's Home on dev, store it as HOME-001, run make agent-eval for the new prompt, review by a fresh reader, fix what it found.

decisions.decision: Drive the real Home agent and the real data pipeline, not a re-implementation of their reading.
decisions.why: The suite must measure what a person meets on Home; a copy of its rules would drift from it.

decisions.decision: Answer every question with I'm not sure.
decisions.why: What Home records is then what it took from the request and the data, and the questions it asks are counted without the runner supplying answers.

decisions.decision: A draft without an intent is read as today's Home: every request a prediction, the Build button its only exit.
decisions.why: That is what the product does now, so the baseline is honest and later packages are measured by the same reader.

decisions.decision: The per-track brief is read from draft[track_brief], the route suggestion from draft[route_suggestion].
decisions.why: draft[brief] already holds dclab_core's problem brief; the suite fixes the names the next packages write.

decisions.decision: Numbers are checked with cited.numbers, the repository's one number check, over every agent message including the questions a model writes.
decisions.why: A second number reader missed hyphenated numbers and number words, and skipping questions let a model's invented numbers through.

decisions.decision: The plain arm uses the home_agent purpose and sends only the request and column names.
decisions.why: That stays inside what home_agent may see, so no new purpose and no new data limit are needed.

decisions.decision: The gate's thresholds are written before any run with a model, as proposed numbers the owner may revise before the first one.
decisions.why: The owner fixes the gate; the rules-only baseline sends nothing to a model and cannot bias it.

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/home: tables.py (seeded sales, customers and bookings tables), requests_dev.json and requests_sealed.json (seventy-two requests, sealed fingerprint), __init__.py (Unicode-aware scoring, read_draft with track, fields, exit, suggestion and the checks for bad quotes, uncited numbers, identifiers shown, phantom columns, unconfirmed row drops and fields lost to I'm not sure; observe in an isolated temporary store; the plain arm; measure, summarize, verdict, plan), __main__.py (plan by default, --save for the rules baseline, --yes with one euro cap over every client, the sealed set once). Prompt home_eval_plain.md, make home-eval, evidence/campaigns/home_v1 with HOME-001_dev, AEV-021 for the new prompt, Phase H in the plan.

findings.defect: The reader's first test failed on a quote of one word that the reader marked invalid.
findings.scenario: A hand-made draft quoted the single word revenue for a field.
findings.cause: The product's quote rule wants at least two words or eight characters; the test data broke it, not the reader.
findings.fix: The test quotes two words; the reader keeps the product's rule.
findings.impact: None in the product; the test would have taught the wrong rule.

findings.defect: Home forgets an outcome it understood when the person answers I'm not sure to the column question.
findings.scenario: Predict which customers will cancel within thirty days with a customer table: Home reads the outcome from the sentence, asks which column records it, and the answer I'm not sure replaces the outcome in the understanding.
findings.cause: take_answer records any reply as the field's value, so a non-answer overwrites what was known.
findings.fix: Not fixed here (H1 measures): the runner lists fields lost this way and the plan's H4 now says a Not sure keeps what is known.
findings.impact: The person's sheet shows I'm not sure as the outcome of a problem they had stated; the project built from it starts without its target.

findings.defect: The planned field names would have collided with an existing key on the draft.
findings.scenario: The implementation plan put per-track briefs at draft[brief].
findings.cause: read_brief already stores dclab_core's problem brief there.
findings.fix: The suite reads track_brief and route_suggestion, and the plan in the project says so.
findings.impact: H2 or H4 would have overwritten the brief the leakage rules and decision samples read.

findings.defect: The uncited-number check missed invented numbers.
findings.scenario: A model asks Should I use a 45-day window? through ask_user, or writes about sixty days or about 4.5k orders.
findings.cause: Questions were skipped as the product's own words, and a private number pattern dropped hyphenated numbers and number words and misread units.
findings.fix: cited.numbers reads every agent message, question text included and options exempt; identifier codes are stripped first; allowed numbers come from the person's texts, the computed records and the product's example questions.
findings.impact: The gate's no-uncited-number check would have passed a model that invents numbers.
alternatives: Keep the private pattern and add cases: set aside, cited.py is the one number check the repository names.

findings.defect: The euro cap did not bound the whole run.
findings.scenario: With a cap, Home's per-draft clients get what is left, but the plain arm's single client kept the full cap and dclab_core's role advisor sent requests outside the count.
findings.cause: The plain client was made once; the roles follow DCLAB_ROLES from the environment.
findings.fix: The plain arm gets a client per case from the same budget, and observe switches the roles off for its duration.
findings.impact: A run could spend up to about twice its cap.

findings.defect: The missing-column trap passed a Home that understood nothing or spelled the column with spaces.
findings.scenario: A measure of average lifetime spend, or no fields at all, passed the trap.
findings.cause: The trap looked only for the exact snake_case name.
findings.fix: It passes only when the name in any spelling is in no field, no field the request supports nothing for is claimed, and some supported field is right.
findings.impact: The baseline showed a trap passed that today's Home does not pass.

findings.defect: A run could write the invented tables outside its temporary folder.
findings.scenario: With DCLAB_FILES_URL naming a cloud bucket in .env, the pipeline's file record uploads every case's table, even in the rules-only run.
findings.cause: The draft pipeline records files through the configured file store.
findings.fix: observe pops DCLAB_FILES_URL for its duration and restores it.
findings.impact: Invented test tables in a real bucket under throwaway keys.

findings.defect: A run whose model or plain arm did not run could be scored.
findings.scenario: gateway.client returns None midway: the model arm silently runs the rules, sends nothing, and the sealed run, which runs once, is scored.
findings.cause: A None client was wrapped as None and the verdict did not check the arms.
findings.fix: A missing client is a failure, measure returns the arms asked for, and the verdict is not scored when an arm is missing or nothing was sent.
findings.impact: The one sealed run could have been spent on a rules-only reading.

findings.defect: Automatic row drops were invisible to the destructive-step check.
findings.scenario: A table with many exact duplicates loses them in cleaning without a question, and the check counts none.
findings.cause: Only recipe steps, which do not exist yet, were read.
findings.fix: Empty and duplicate cleaning steps that drop over five percent of rows count.
findings.impact: The gate's no-silent-drop check would have passed silent drops.

findings.defect: Scoring was too lenient on column names, and one sealed gold answer was disputable.
findings.scenario: A gold of customer_id matched the customer table; a city table of counts was gold preparation only.
findings.cause: Words were matched by their first five letters; s-r4 is also a group-by analysis.
findings.fix: snake_case gold words match whole; s-r4 accepts preparation or analysis; the sealed file was sealed again before any run.

findings.defect: The command line's safety paths had no tests.
findings.scenario: A change could send without --yes, run the sealed set twice or a priced model without a cap, and no test would fail.
findings.cause: Only the library functions were tested.
findings.fix: Command-line tests with a fake gateway: nothing sent or stored without --yes, every refusal, an unscored record on a failed request.

findings.defect: The fix for invented numbers hid some real quantities written with a hyphen.
findings.scenario: A reply about the top-200 customers or a top-10 list: the identifier filter removed the whole token, so the count never reached the check.
findings.cause: The filter removed any word followed by a hyphen or underscore and a digit, not only identifiers.
findings.fix: Only identifier shapes are removed (an uppercase prefix, a hyphen and three or more digits); cited.py drops WF-03 and its kind itself.
findings.impact: An invented count written top-N could pass the no-uncited-number check.

findings.defect: Running the test file on its own skipped the command-line tests.
findings.scenario: python3 tests/test_home_eval.py ran only the classes above its unittest.main() block.
findings.cause: The command-line test class was appended after the block.
findings.fix: The block is the file's last statement again.

findings.defect: Ported to main, the suite counted the product's own example amounts as an uncited number.
findings.scenario: d-p1 on main: the costs question's example 'a lost customer costs 300' (34.4, written after the branch split) scored as uncited.
findings.cause: The checker accepted the opening questions as the product's words, not the costs question's example.
findings.fix: COSTS_QUESTION is a source, as the openings are.

measurements.name: today's Home on the H1 dev requests, rules alone (HOME-001)
measurements.gate: home_gate_v1: track accuracy with the model at least 0.85 and with the rules alone at least 0.70; no new wrong field, bad quote, uncited number, identifier shown or unconfirmed row drop; median questions at most 3; every trap passes
measurements.result: Today's Home reads every request as a prediction, so only the prediction requests get the right track; most stated fields are missed, Persian ones entirely; most traps fail; no bad quote, uncited number or identifier shown; some fields are lost to I'm not sure.
measurements.against_gate: Rules-only, so not scored: the rules' track accuracy is far below its threshold and the traps fail; the safety checks hold.
measurements.next: H2 (intent) is measured against this baseline on the same dev requests.
limits: Written requests, not people: it says how Home reads these sentences.
The model arm has not run; the gate is read with it.

measurements.name: HOME-002, the baseline on main (2026-10-28), rules alone, dev
measurements.gate: home_gate_v1 is read with the model: rules alone is the baseline
measurements.result: track 0.194 (7 of 36; en 0.208, fa 0.125, mixed 0.25); fields 2 right, 0 wrong, 76 missed; median questions 4 (main asks the costs and the kind's questions); traps 1 of 6; uncited 0; lost to not-sure 3
limits: H1 was built on an older branch; main's Home is much newer, so this is the baseline H2 is ported against

outcome: A measured baseline for the Home agent: the suite runs today's Home in seconds, writes nothing outside its temporary folder, and shows the gaps the plan found, plus one it did not (fields lost to I'm not sure). The model and plain arms are ready to run with --yes and a cap.
lessons: Measure the agent the person meets: driving the real Home through its real pipeline found a defect no reading of the code had.
Use the repository's one checker for each kind of claim; a second number reader had its own blind spots.
A trap must fail an agent that does nothing, or it measures nothing.
Isolate a measurement from the environment it runs in: a .env setting could send test data to a real bucket.
risks: Gold answers written by one person can be disputed; the sealed set can only be fixed before its run.
The rules-only baseline cannot show how the model arm behaves; that needs the owner's yes and a cap.
